A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RFM/DIP method and LRS-VQA benchmark, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends after references despite appendix cross-references; v3 supplies Supplementary Sections A–D. This supports comparison of newly documented material without assuming changes to previously unspecified implementation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA evaluations, token-reduction comparisons, efficiency measurements and ablations in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds localization evaluations, further ablations and detailed benchmark results in the supplement.

M1.justification: The DIP construction, RFM architecture, distillation losses and Algorithm 1 are retained. Supplementary implementation explanations do not establish a changed method. Training-time pruning, text fusion and multi-level token concatenation are tested alternatives, not replacements for the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds localization evaluation using DIOR-RSVG and RRSIS-D, plus region-box localization tests on LRS-VQA. This extends v1's VQA evaluation to directly assessing text-guided region coverage. The original training datasets and four VQA evaluation sets remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds CLIP-L14 and RemoteCLIP-L14 sliding-window pruning baselines to main Table 3 and supplementary comparisons. Teacher LLM attention also becomes a comparator in localization evaluation. These substantially broaden tests of the central guidance mechanism; the original LVLM and token-reduction comparators remain.

E3.justification: New localization tests use 25% token retention and count success when retained tokens cover over 50% of the ground-truth region. Added controlled experiments introduce anyres-p36/p49, further layer configurations, training-time pruning and text fusion. Original VQA metrics and documented main settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative attention-localization validation and ablations of distillation losses, pruning at larger resolutions, concatenating tokens across pyramid levels, and training with pruning/text fusion. v1's layer-pair ablation is retained and expanded in supplementary Table 6, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing headline scores are retained, including the 32.16 average for Ours (LLaVA-Next) in Table 2. v3 adds RFM localization recalls of 47.99%, 64.76% and 61.17% on LRS-VQA, DIOR-RSVG and RRSIS-D, respectively, alongside new baseline scores, ablation outcomes and per-question-category leaderboards.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds explicit token-count and FLOPs derivations for the pyramid/RFM/LLM computation, culminating in the previously reported 36.61 TFLOPs. The original method equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same RFM/DIP proposal, architecture-agnostic accuracy/efficiency claims, and 7,333-pair, eight-category LRS-VQA contribution. New experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantial explanations and qualifications: CLIP baselines' referring-expression and global-context limitations, incomplete visual information as an explanation for training-pruning degradation, and interference from mixing resolutions. The supplement also discusses long-context constraints, text-fusion inconsistency, vocabulary sensitivity and why higher resolution need not help global classification.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C supply previously unavailable construction thresholds, annotation prompts, training-data processing, batch size 128, learning rate 2e-5, sequence-length limits, positional-padding details, Flash Attention extraction, caching and compute accounting. These materially expand reproducibility information without demonstrating that the retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds an adaptive/superpixel tokenization thread, references for CLIP/RemoteCLIP and localization datasets, and additional remote-sensing works such as SkySense and MEET; SkyEyeGPT is removed. The main research taxonomy and positioning relative to LLaVA-Mini and FlexAttention remain.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Section 4.1 gains clearer coarse-to-fine transitions, experimental discussion is reorganized, and layer-pair discussion moves into the new supplement. Author affiliations, contact information and acknowledgments also change; the main manuscript is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 retain their visual content. However, Table 3 expands, a localization table occupies main Table 7, and the original layer-pair table moves into an expanded supplementary display. The supplement adds a prompt box and numerous ablation, localization and category-level tables, substantially expanding the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves important validation and documentation gaps: direct localization comparisons test the central distillation rationale, additional ablations examine design choices and failures, and Appendices A–C make construction and implementation substantially easier to audit. These gains matter despite unchanged headline performance. Appendix C introduces a limited inconsistency between the 2ndm feed-forward term in prose and 3ndm in its equation, but this does not outweigh the stronger evidence and reproducibility documentation.
